name: The Humane League: grants to Open Wing Alliance groups, THL UK and US policy groups (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: by share of the result (chicken pain days) at the defaults: the grant to THL UK (UK commitments, switches, the cage ban and the breed case, 86%), the US policy grants (1%), and the Open Wing Alliance grants abroad (12%) split by Schedule F's grant regions (Sub-Saharan Africa 30%, South America 26%, Europe outside the UK 25%, East Asia 9%, Middle East and North Africa 6%, South Asia 4%), each region at a stand-in country (Ghana, Brazil, Poland, Indonesia, Egypt, India; the review names wins in Ghana and Indonesia, the 990 in Poland).
summary: The Humane League's grants of 2025 ($4.26 million), each counted as what the recipients did with the money: $1.76 million to Open Wing Alliance groups abroad for corporate cage-free and broiler campaigns (credited with the grants' share of the alliance's 2025 wins outside the US: 216 new cage-free policies, restored pledges such as REWE's, 18 broiler policies implemented), $2.15 million to The Humane League UK (Tesco's and Aldi's space commitments for 240 million broilers a year, won in its year and delivered since, UK hens moved out of cages, and its part in a UK cage ban and in the legal case against fast-growing breeds, both counted at their chance), and $0.35 million to US policy groups (defending state cage-free sales laws against federal preemption, and local food-policy wins). The result is below the site's animal-welfare median: each grant buys a small share of wins that many groups share, and every branch rests on counts or chances we judged, so all are discounted for missing data. The biggest uncertainties are how much more space does for a broiler of a fast-growing breed (the UK space commitments are two thirds of the result), THL UK's share of the supermarket campaigns, the long shot of the breed case, and the hens behind an average new pledge abroad.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model. The shared SAD figures are Ambitious Impact's, which count each species' pain as a share of a person's with its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken compares with a person is the one animal slider.

rows.label: New cage-free policies won by Open Wing Alliance members, 2025

source.title: Open Wing Alliance, 2025 end-of-year review (The Humane League, 18 February 2026)
source.quote: 216 new cage-free policies are now secured, helping egg-laying hens out of cages

rows.explainer: The alliance's count for 2025 (with 18 broiler policies implemented, the 990's '234 new corporate commitments for chickens', more than 60 in Africa).

rows.label: Share of the alliance's wins outside the US
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The alliance's 82 members work in 72 countries; THL's own new US commitments were four ('spare 1.6 million hens around the world', 990 Part III), and the review's named wins are in Ghana, Indonesia, Latvia and Europe. US wins belong to THL's own campaigns (another line), so they are taken out here and from the staff count below alike.

rows.label: Hens a year covered by an average new policy
rows.explainer: Our judgment: no tracker gives hens for the 216 policies. Anchors: the largest named, Agro Innova in Ghana, distributes about 15 million eggs a month (about 600,000 hens at some 300 eggs a hen-year); THL's four new commitments covered 1.6 million hens (large US and European firms); most of the alliance's policies are hotels, bakeries, restaurants and regional producers with a few thousand hens each. A skewed mix averages about 10,000.

rows.label: Share of those hens not yet cage-free when the policy was won
rows.explainer: Our judgment: outside the EU, UK and US nearly all hens are caged (Welfare Footprint's country compilation in Our World in Data's cage-free series), but some companies pledge when they already buy some cage-free eggs.

rows.label: Hens a year under the new pledges abroad, not yet cage-free
Share of the hens abroad in enriched rather than battery cages
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on Schedule F: Europe outside the UK took $426,310 of the $1.69 million of listed grants abroad (25%), and the EU has used enriched cages since 2012; Africa, Latin America and Asia use battery cages. Policies in Europe are fewer per dollar than in the Global South, hence 20%.

rows.label: Chance a cage ban becomes law (England, then the devolved nations)

source.title: The Humane League UK, An historic moment for farmed animals (22 December 2025)
source.quote: A consultation is not a ban, but it is a critical step forward.

rows.explainer: Our judgment. The government's Animal Welfare Strategy (22 December 2025) committed to consult on ending cages, and the consultation opened in January 2026 with a six-year phase-out; consultations usually lead to rules, but the egg industry opposes the timeline and parliamentary time is short. One event, drawn as happening or not.

rows.label: Chance the legal route ends fast-growing breeds in the UK

source.title: The Humane League UK, annual report and accounts, year to 31 March 2025
source.quote: they ruled in favour of our main argument - that the law says that animals should not be kept in the UK if it means they will suffer because of how they have been bred

rows.explainer: Our judgment. The Court of Appeal rejected THL UK's appeal but agreed that the law forbids keeping animals that suffer because of how they were bred; THL UK plans private prosecutions on that reading. Such cases rarely change a whole industry: about 1 in 30 within the years counted. One event, drawn as happening or not.

rows.label: Chance federal preemption of the state sales laws passes, without the year's opposition

source.title: The Humane League, Animal Policy Alliance year in review (1 February 2026)
source.quote: By the end of the year, more than 200 members of Congress had signed letters opposing the EATS language

rows.explainer: Our judgment. The EATS Act's language and the 'Save Our Bacon' Act were in the House Farm Bill drafts of 2024-25; the coalition (Humane World for Animals, ASPCA, THL and the APA groups) gathered letters from more than 200 members of Congress against them. Without that opposition we put passage in the next Farm Bill at 30%; drawn together with the chance with it (one event).

rows.label: Chance federal preemption passes, with the year's opposition
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the year's opposition takes about 5 points off (a sixth of the risk). The same event as the row above, drawn so it happens with the opposition only when it would without.

rows.label: Staff of alliance members working on cage-free and broiler campaigns

source.title: Open Wing Alliance, 2025 end-of-year review
source.quote: More than 525 staff focused on cage-free and broiler welfare

rows.explainer: The alliance's own count for 2025.

rows.label: Share of those staff outside the US
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the large US members (THL, Mercy For Animals, Animal Equality US and others) employ perhaps a hundred to two hundred campaigners on hens and broilers; the other 70-odd members are abroad.

rows.label: Cost of a campaigner abroad a year, with the group's other costs
rows.explainer: Our judgment: THL UK spends about $83,000 a staff member (£1.68m for 26), groups in Latin America, Africa and Asia a fraction of that; a mix weighted to the Global South.

rows.label: THL's own spending on running the alliance (staff, trainings, Fair and Fowl)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: THL's annual report puts its global programmes at $5.2 million including the THL UK grant; the alliance's team, four regional summits and trainings, mentorship and the Fair and Fowl report are about a third of the rest.

rows.label: All resources behind the alliance's wins abroad, 2025
rows.explainer: Members' campaign staff abroad (paid partly by these grants, partly by other funders, whose money is therefore already here) and THL's own running of the alliance. With credit by share of resources, the pay the members' campaigners forgo counts as their in-kind share too (the shared advocacy pay share and gap).

rows.label: The grants' share of the resources behind the alliance's wins abroad
rows.explainer: Credit by share of resources (Convention 2): the wins of 2025 are shared over everything spent on them, and the grants get their share.

rows.label: Share of new pledges abroad later pressed by accountability work
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the Fair and Fowl report and the alliance's trackers follow the larger companies, so about half the hens under a new pledge later get pressed.

rows.label: The grant as a share of THL UK's yearly resources
rows.explainer: THL UK's outcomes of its audited year are credited to the grant in proportion to the grant's share of a year's spending (about nine tenths). With credit by share of resources, the pay THL UK's campaigners forgo (the shared advocacy pay gap, as for the alliance's members and THL's own staff) is a resource too.

rows.label: THL UK's share of the campaigners' resources behind the space commitments
rows.explainer: Our judgment: THL UK has run the supermarket campaigns (Co-op's AGM, Lidl's 'Shop of Horrors', Tesco) with Open Cages, Animal Equality UK, the RSPCA and Compassion in World Farming also pressing for better broiler standards.

rows.label: THL UK's share of the resources pressing UK cage-free pledges
rows.explainer: Our judgment: THL UK's corporate relations team, Compassion in World Farming's EggTrack and the RSPCA all follow UK pledges.

rows.label: THL UK's year's share of all resources behind a cage ban
rows.explainer: Our judgment: about ten groups (Compassion in World Farming, the RSPCA, Humane World for Animals UK, Four Paws, Animal Equality, Open Cages, the Conservative Animal Welfare Foundation, THL UK) over some five years; THL UK's public affairs is one post and its supporters' emails.

rows.label: THL UK's year's share of all resources behind a legal end to fast-growing breeds
rows.explainer: Our judgment: THL UK brought the case (with Advocates for Animals) and the appeal fell in its year; a later win would need further cases and the other groups' work.

rows.label: The APA grants' share of all resources opposing preemption in 2025
rows.explainer: Our judgment: a part of the $351,300 went to federal work (the Missouri Alliance for Animal Legislation, Strategic Action for Animals), beside Humane World for Animals', the ASPCA's and THL's own lobbying, millions of dollars a year.

rows.label: The APA grants' share of the resources behind the food-policy wins
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the grants paid for the grantees' campaigns (Compassionate Action for Animals' Hennepin County default was named as grant-funded); students, the MSPCA, the Plant Powered School Meals Coalition and others did much of the work.

rows.label: New pledges abroad: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the policy count is the alliance's own, checked against Chicken Watch's public pledges; some policies cover only part of a company's eggs (shell eggs, one country).

rows.label: New pledges abroad: share that wouldn't have come yet without the work
rows.explainer: New pledges later pressed: the share of their switches credited to that later pressure is taken off here (templates.md, corporate-campaign accountability). That a pledge would have come anyway later is the shared years counted.

rows.label: New pledges abroad: the grant's share of the resources behind it
New pledges abroad: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The grant's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: New pledges abroad: share of commitments kept
rows.explainer: The site's one rate of cage-free pledges kept (a pledge only helps hens if kept).

rows.label: New pledges abroad: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): no one measured what this work changed for animals against what would have happened without it; the reach or the effect here rests on judgment.

rows.label: New pledges abroad: all adjustments combined
Pledges restored abroad: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: Our judgment: REWE's hens and progress are its own figures; the other wins' hens are our judgment.

rows.label: Pledges restored abroad: share that wouldn't have come yet without the work
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the share of these switches that wouldn't have come yet without the pressure.
